title: The Guide Now Fills Quiet Roads With the Area's Story | vitalii.no
description:
The guide only ever talked about specific places tied to a GPS coordinate — the moment a stretch of road had no tagged place ahead, it went silent for minutes at a time. That was true even though the surrounding district often has a rich, sourced history: old trades, place-name origins, railway lines — none of it ever told because it isn't pinned to a single point.

A new runner/zone.py script fetches zone-level sources — lokalhistoriewiki, Wikipedia, SNL articles, and OCR text from public-domain National Library scans, including Helland's 1913 book on Toten and Rygh's 1902 farm-names book — plus the district's place names from Kartverket. Using Claude, the guide now writes up to eight bilingual episodes about the area's history, roads, railways, trades and place-names then-and-now, and plays one whenever nothing specific is due on the road ahead.

Long quiet stretches of driving now get up to 8 chained, sourced episodes about the district instead of silence, built from two digitized 1902 and 1913 books that had no prior digital narration at all.
